$comment: R1738 — WHICH SECTIONS OF THE ASSEMBLED APPLICATION ARE JUDGED, and for
each that is not, the reason that was accepted.
WHAT THIS PIN IS A CLAIM ABOUT, AND WHAT IT IS NOT. The sibling pins
(`analyzer-rail-spec.json`, `analyzer-keys-spec.json`,
`analyzer-logs-spec.json`, `analyzer-inspector-spec.json`,
`analyzer-board-spec.json`) are claims about the BEHAVIOUR REFERENCE —
what it draws, in neutral vocabulary, written from an extraction. This one
is not. It is a claim about THIS BUILD: of the sections the reference
opens, which ones this application can currently say anything about.
It therefore does not repeat the seat list. The population is
`analyzer-rail-spec.json`'s canon, read from there, and this file holds
only the remainder — because a second copy of the eight seats is how two
screens of this tool came to disagree about what the tool contains, and
the fix for that was not another list.
WHAT FORCED IT. Measured over the wire at R1738, standing in each section
of the running application in turn: the application's own `conformance`
slot answered `specified 8, reproduced 8` from every one of them. That is
true about the RAIL. Read as a statement about the tool — which is how it
reads — it was wrong: two of the six open sections published a verdict
about their own surfaces, four published nothing, and no slot, test or
report anywhere named the other four. They were not failing a check; they
were absent from the population.
HOW IT IS ENFORCED. `scene`-side, `ScreenRoster::conformance` builds one
row per destination FROM THE ROSTER, so a section is missing from the
report only by not being in the application. Gate-side, the entries below
are asserted EQUAL to the application's unjudged rows — so a section that
starts answering must have its entry DELETED here, and an entry left
behind fails exactly as loudly as a section that went silent. A remainder
list that only ever grows is a remainder list nobody reads.
THE TWO KINDS BELOW ARE DIFFERENT WORK. `inline` is a page the host paints
itself and nothing answers for; `unspecified` is a mounted screen that
publishes no verdict.
★★★★★ R1761 CORRECTED WHAT THIS FILE SAID CLOSING AN `inline` ENTRY MEANS.
It read: *closing it means giving that page a `Screen` of its own, which is
what the trait being public is for*, copied from the framework type that
said the same. Both were written from the type rather than from a
measurement, and both were wrong in the direction that costs most — they
named a route so expensive that neither entry was closed for twenty-three
rounds, and the route would not have worked.
Measured on the running application at R1761, standing on `dashboard`: the
page region a screen would be granted is 1096x802 at (52, 98), while that
section's layout bar is 1096x46 at (52, 52) and its palette is 292x848 at
(1148, 52). A host paints a section's chrome BESIDE the page region because
that is what chrome is, and a screen judges what it paints — so the
recorded route would have shipped a verdict blind to a quarter of its own
section, and blind to the surface that section is most distinctive for.
The route is now `ScreenRoster::judging`: a judge for a page the host
paints, which answers how much of a written specification is on the frame
and grants nothing else. Becoming a `Screen` is still the move for a page
that wants a screen's BEHAVIOUR; it is no longer the price of saying a true
sentence about a page.
R1742 CLOSED `lab`, which was the second kind of `unspecified` — a screen
with a written specification it compared itself against inside a unit test
of its own binary, where the assembled application could not see it. Its
entry is DELETED rather than marked done, because the entries here are
asserted equal to the application's unjudged rows and a paid entry left
behind fails as loudly as a section that went silent. What made it the
hardest of the four is what the round had to decide: its surfaces exist
only once a session has selected a card and opened a roster, so its verdict
is about a session rather than about the build. A screen now says which of
its specified surfaces are NOT ON SCREEN and why, that count is part of the
verdict, and a report holding one does not reconcile — so the honesty is
structural rather than a promise. See `pinion_core::conformance::Built`.
★★★★★ R1747 CLOSED `packets`, AND CORRECTED WHAT THIS FILE SAID ABOUT IT.
The deleted entry read: *the capture viewer has no written specification at
all — not one unpublished, one unwritten*. That sentence was FALSE when
R1738 wrote it and stayed false for nine rounds. Re-measured 2026-08-20 by
listing the crate's modules and grepping the tree for the hook: R1663 wrote
screen B's specification as a value in that crate's `spec` module and its
`painted` module already ran the real view and layout passes and compared
the painted scene against it in both directions. Both predate the entry.
What was true is the OTHER half of the same sentence — those modules are
`#[cfg(test)]` and the binding implemented no `conformance` hook — so this
was *one unpublished*, the same shape `lab` was in, and the entry misnamed
which of the two kinds it was.
The lesson is the one this project keeps paying for and it is written here
rather than only in a round's ledger: A REASON RECORDED IN A REMAINDER IS
NOT RE-MEASURED BY THE THING THAT ENFORCES IT. The gate below asserts the
KEYS equal the application's unjudged rows and can say nothing at all about
the `why` beside them, so a wrong reason survives every push that a right
one would. Anything acting on one of these entries re-measures it first.
Both remaining entries are the `inline` kind, so the `unspecified` kind now
has no live case. The bottom remainder stays open anyway: the type is
unchanged, and the next screen with a specification it cannot publish yet
would be silent in exactly the same way.
★★★★★ R1888 CHANGED THE TYPE, which is what that last paragraph was
waiting for. `SectionStanding::Unspecified` carries the screen's own
sentence now, and a screen that has not written one hands back an
admission the report COUNTS (`unaccounted`) rather than a plausible
default that would have passed every check for having said something. The
bottom remainder's first entry is deleted; see `it_is_the_application`'s
own comment for what was built and for the mutations that showed each gate
red.
★★★★★ R1762 — THIS LIST IS EMPTY, and that is what R1738 opened the
count for: every section of the assembled application a reader can
arrive at is now compared with a written specification, and the
application says so itself (`unjudged: 0`, measured over the wire).
It took five rounds and each closed a different kind of thing. R1742
made a screen publish a verdict it already computed. R1747 corrected a
reason that had been false for nine rounds and published a second. R1758
made a verdict say what it was read from. R1761 found that the route
recorded for the last two was itself wrong — a host paints a section's
chrome beside the page region, so a `Screen` there would judge three
quarters of its own section — and built the smaller thing instead.
R1762 could then write the last pin, once the page it is about had the
three rows, the heading and the footer the reference draws and this
build did not.
AN EMPTY LIST IS STILL ASSERTED. The gate compares these entries with
the application's unjudged rows as an EQUALITY, so a section that stops
answering fails here as loudly as an entry left behind after it was
paid. Empty is a claim, not an absence of one.
★★★★★ R1888 CLOSED `a-section-cannot-say-why-it-answers-nothing`. Its
entry is DELETED rather than marked done, for the reason every entry in
this file is: a paid remainder left behind reads exactly like an unpaid
one, and this list is only worth reading if it shrinks.
What it said: *an unjudged section's row carries the host's reason, not
the screen's* — `SectionStanding::Unspecified` was a unit variant, so
`why()` answered one constant sentence for every such section, and the
two facts it stood in for (nobody wrote a specification / one exists
where the assembled application cannot reach it) are known only to the
screen. The entry named its own repair: *a declared absence that carries
its reason, the way a closed destination's does — the shape to copy is
one level down in the same module*. That is `Built::Away`, and it is
what was built: the arm carries a `String`, `Screen::unjudged_because`
is asked exactly when `conformance` answers nothing, and `Mount`
forwards the binding's own sentence.
★★★★★ AND THE HALF THE ENTRY DID NOT NAME, which is what took the round
rather than the edit: the binding hook has to be DEFAULTED, because most
bindings in this tree are not sections of anything. A default is an
escape hatch, and an escape hatch that reads like an answer disables the
check it lives under. So the default is `pinion_shell::UNSTATED`, worded
as an ADMISSION rather than an explanation, and `ApplicationConformance`
counts it: `unaccounted`, published beside `unjudged` and per row as
`accounts`. Unaccounted is a strict subset of unjudged, so it moves
nothing about conformance — what it buys is the finer word. A silence
with a reason is a known gap with an address; a silence without one is a
gap nobody has looked at, and one count cannot send a reader to both
repairs.
⚠ THE POPULATION IS EMPTY IN THIS BUILD and that is not the same as the
mechanism being untested. `unjudged` is 0 here, so no section is
`unspecified` at all — the precedent for what to do about that is in
this file already, written by R1762 into the demo it made vacuous: the
rule is measured where a fixture can hold an unjudged section on
purpose, and the assembled application asserts the equality. So
`pinion-screen`'s own fixtures stand on both sides of the distinction
(one silent screen that explains itself, one that has not), the shell
asserts `unaccounted_keys()` empty, and R1888's walk asserts it over the
wire from every section in turn. All three were shown red by mutation,
and the end-to-end one twice: a mounted screen made silent reported
`unjudged 1, unaccounted 1`, and the same screen given a sentence
reported `unjudged 1, unaccounted 0` — the two counts coming apart in
the running tool, which is the whole claim.
★★★★★ R1911 CLOSED `a-verdict-is-not-recomputed-per-frame`, AND THE
MEASUREMENT REFUTED BOTH HALVES OF IT. Its entry is DELETED rather than
marked done, for this file's standing reason. What it said: *the report
is built on demand and nothing caches or invalidates it*, that four
sections now `include_str!` + JSON-parse a pin per read, and — in its
own words — that calling it cheap was *an argument from where it is
called, not a measurement of what it costs*. It asked to be measured.
It was.
Isolated one variable at a time, release profile, on this machine:
a pin parse                                          13.6 us
a clone of the parsed document                        1.0 us
/external/nav          (9 bytes, builds nothing)     284.0 us
/external/destinations (2,395 bytes)                 213.8 us
/external/sections     (27,384 bytes, THE REPORT)  1,262.4 us
/external/spec         (42,836 bytes, A CONSTANT) 1,636.6 us
⇒ FOUR PINS PARSED PER READ IS ~54 us, 4% OF THE READ. The entry's
named repair — the parsed document behind a `OnceCell` — would have
bought 4% and cost five call sites. And the dominant term is not the
report at all: `/external/spec` BUILDS NOTHING, ships 42.8 KB and costs
1,636.6 us, so at that slot's own rate 27.4 KB predicts ~1,111 us of the
1,262.4 us measured. What a report read costs is what it SHIPS.
⚠ THE RESIDUE, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. 1.26 ms is 7.5% of a 60 Hz
frame, so if this report were ever read per frame it would matter — and
caching the verdict would not fix it, because the term is serialisation.
Nothing reads it per frame today: it is a wire slot at an agent's
cadence, which is now a measurement rather than an argument.
⚠ AND THE ONE THIS FILE CANNOT FIX: `it_is_the_application.owed` is
hand-kept and NO CODE READS IT (measured again at R1911: zero matches
for `it_is_the_application` across tools, crates, examples and hooks),
unlike `unjudged.owed`, which six files assert equality against. That is
registered as its own open debt rather than left as a sentence here.

What an ungated list costs, measured the same round: the entry below
was DELETED from this file while the thing it describes was still
true. `SpecDocument::pinned` parses its text on every call and the
verdict path calls it per read, exactly as the entry says — so a live
remainder left silently, which is the whole failure mode of a list
`refuted_by` is the shape that fixes it: a needle that will APPEAR in
the tree when the remainder is paid. The gate refuses an entry whose
needle is present — meaning the work is done and the entry must be
deleted — so this list can only shrink, and it cannot shrink quietly.

owed.sentence: the report is built on demand and nothing caches or invalidates it
why: Every read walks the roster and asks each mounted screen, and each
one builds its document by PARSING its pinned text again:
`SpecDocument::pinned` calls `parse` with no memoisation, and the
verdict path calls it per read. It is a wire read at an agent's
cadence rather than a paint-time cost, so it is not on any frame
budget measured so far — but that is an argument from where it is
called, not a measurement of what it costs.
R2043 re-measured both halves before restoring this: the parse is
still per call, and no memoising cell exists anywhere on a verdict
path (the four in this tree all belong to one screen's settings
module). The entry was deleted while both were still true.
